Fill the level combinations that the fitted rows do not identify

Source: R/cellgloc_utils.R
dot-gloc_fill_null.Rd

Returns \(b = b_0 + N c\). Identified combinations keep their fitted means, because \(p N = 0\) for their pure design rows \(p\); a row whose categories are unknown gets whatever its design row gives with the filled coefficients. The fill runs in two stages. First, \(c\) is the minimum-norm least-squares solution of \(p (b_0 + N c) = t_p\) over the unidentified combinations that occur in the data. Second, the unidentified combinations absent from the data are fitted the same way, but only in the directions of the null space that the first stage leaves free, which are invisible on every combination of the first stage. An absent combination therefore never changes the fitted mean of a row that exists, and the same data give the same fitted means whether or not absent combinations are enumerated (.gloc_max_patterns). (Corrected: until the third 7.4.1 fix round both kinds entered one least-squares step, and absent combinations moved present ones: under partial aliasing imputed values changed by up to 1.80.) Each stage divides only by singular values above .gloc_est_tol times the length of the longest pure row involved, so finite input gives finite coefficients under any contrasts. With no unidentified combination, \(b_0\) is returned as it is.

.gloc_fill_null(b0, P, est, target, present = rep(TRUE, nrow(P)))

Arguments

b0

length-\(q\) coefficients of the fit, 0 in the aliased columns.

P

the pure design rows of the combinations.

est

the result of .gloc_estimable.

target

one target value per combination; only unidentified ones are read.

present

logical, one element per combination, from .gloc_present.

Value

length-\(q\) coefficients.
